name: Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party
description: The Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party (YSRCP) is a regional political party based in Andhra Pradesh. Founded in 2011 by Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy after separating from the Indian National Congress, the party is named after his father and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy (YSR). YSRCP focuses on welfare governance, farmers' welfare, healthcare, education, social justice and inclusive development. The party formed the government in Andhra Pradesh from 2019 to 2024 under Jagan Mohan Reddy.
achievements: Formed the Andhra Pradesh government in 2019 with a strong majority.
Implemented large-scale welfare schemes under the Navaratnalu programme.
Expanded direct benefit transfer schemes for citizens.
Introduced Amma Vodi scheme providing financial assistance to mothers for children's education.
Implemented YSR Rythu Bharosa for farmer support.
Expanded healthcare access through YSR Aarogyasri scheme.
Focused on village-level governance through Village and Ward Secretariats.
Introduced reforms in government schools through Nadu-Nedu programme.
Promoted women's welfare through financial assistance schemes.
criticisms: Opposition parties criticised the party over state debt and financial management.
Critics questioned the effectiveness and sustainability of welfare schemes.
The party faced criticism regarding the Amaravati capital issue and administrative decisions.
Opponents accused the government of political targeting of rivals.
Critics raised concerns about industrial investment and employment generation.
protests: Campaigns supporting farmers and agricultural welfare.
Movements demanding special category status for Andhra Pradesh.
Protests regarding development and state financial issues.
Public demonstrations on issues affecting Andhra Pradesh's interests.
majorSchemes: Housing for Poor under YSR Housing Scheme
timeline: 2011 - YSR Congress Party founded by Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
2012 - Jagan Mohan Reddy won Kadapa Lok Sabha by-election with a large majority.
2014 - YSRCP became the main opposition party in Andhra Pradesh after state bifurcation.
2019 - YSRCP won Andhra Pradesh Assembly election with a large majority; Jagan Mohan Reddy became Chief Minister.
2021 - Continued implementation of welfare-focused governance programmes.
2023 - Andhra Pradesh politics focused heavily on capital development and welfare debates.
2024 - YSRCP lost Andhra Pradesh Assembly election and became opposition party.
